literalGroups.primaryGround: The current proposed key names Kruger National Park. The official SANParks page identifies itself as South African National Parks (L4) and its content as Kruger National Park (L147-L149); its global game-viewing description is at L197-L199. Retained UNESCO source places Serengeti in Tanzania (L113-L123); retained Namibian Ministry source identifies Etosha as Namibia’s park (L10, L23-L25); TANAPA’s official park page identifies Tarangire under Tanzania National Parks (L10-L17, L158-L166). Thus only Kruger among these four is the South African park.

L13: 
L14: cite17†Explore the Wild L15: ## Wildlife & The Great Elephant Gathering
L16: 
L17: Witness one of Africa’s highest concentrations of elephants, alongside massive herds of wildebeest, zebras, and buffalo during the dry season a spectacular migration rivaled only by its baobab-studded scenery.
L18: 
L19: cite18†Image: Tarangire Wildlife L20: 
L21: ### Lion
L22: 
L23: ### Iconic Wildlife
L24: 
L25: Tarangire is a year-round wildlife paradise, famous for its: 3,000+ elephants (the densest population in Tanzania), Legendary baobab landscapes (some over 1,000 years old).
L26: ### The Ancient Baobabs
L27: 
L28: Tarangire’s "Tree of Life" giants tower over the savanna, some reaching 30 meters tall with trunks over 10 meters wide.
L29: 
L30: ### Termite Mounds & Animal Watchtowers
L31: 
L32: Scattered across the park, these towering mud cathedrals—built by termites and hardened by sun—become lookout posts for lions, cheetahs, and mongoose.
L33:
